label: update gate drops when policy favours a1; extra drop at D1 after a1->S2
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 28 sits near 1 (mean 0.986) and dips mainly late in the episode (timing alone R^2 0.40). Beyond timing, the main driver is the model policy logit (a1 minus a2): z is lower the more the policy favours a1, at every phase, most strongly at D1 (choice alone, three phase-specific terms, dev R^2 beyond timing 0.56). At D1 the effect is nonlinear, with most of the drop at the most-a1 deciles. There are extra D1 drops after a1 that reached S2 (rare), larger when unrewarded (about -0.02) than rewarded (about -0.013), a small extra drop at D1 after any unrewarded trial, and a stronger policy dependence in trials 80+. Full 8-term model: dev 0.70. Uses the model policy output (observable at the step), no future variables. An observed-only version (previous choice a1, a1-S2 patterns at D1, the a1 choice at GO/D2, late-episode a1, D1 unrewarded) gets test 0.55, so the policy logit adds a fair amount. Value and hidden good state add little once the policy is included. Remaining misses are sustained low-z stretches in individual late-episode windows (trials 92-99) that are deeper than the model predicts.

issues: The 8-term model reproduces at test 0.687. The core claim also holds: the three phase-specific policy-logit terms alone score test 0.547.

The D1 nonlinearity is described backwards. The fitted weights are (D1)*choice -0.0031 and (D1)*max(choice,0) +0.0027, so at D1 the slope is about -0.0004 when the policy favours a1 and -0.003 when it favours a2. That means z at D1 is nearly flat across a1-favouring logits and rises as the policy moves toward a2. It does not say 'most of the drop comes in the most-a1 deciles'. The raw decile-8 drop in the profile (-0.017) is taken up by the a1->S2 terms. On its own, max(choice,0) adds nothing (0.5473 -> 0.5476 test); squared or clipped variants reach only 0.551-0.553.

The 'stronger from trial 80' claim is right in direction but the shape is wrong. The late effect is a ramp, not a step. Replacing choice*(ep_trial>=80) with choice*max(ep_trial-80,0), and adding (D1)*(prev_reward==0)*max(ep_trial-80,0), raises test from 0.687 to 0.716, which is above the 'all' additive ceiling of 0.70. The late-episode low-z stretches (trials 92-99) that the explanation dismisses as leftover misses are a systematic error class, and this shape captures much of it.

The a1->S2 extra drop is real and specific: adding the a2->S1 rare transition contributes 0 (0.6870 -> 0.6870). The separate rewarded and unrewarded a1 S2 terms are not needed. A single (D1)*(prev_action==1)*(prev_state==2) term (weight about -0.016), together with the prev_reward==0 term, gives the same result.
Calling a1->S2 'a rare transition' is somewhat misleading: the effect does not generalise to rare transitions. After a2->S2 or a2->S1 trials, the residual at D1 is positive.
The leftover misses by phase and previous trial are small (at most 0.005). The worst is GO after a1 S1 u being over-predicted by -0.005. There are no large non-temporal systematic gaps.
skeptic.revised_label: update gate drops as policy logit favours a1 (all phases; at D1 mainly on the a2 side); extra D1 drop after a1->S2 and after unrewarded trials; both effects ramp up after trial 80
